g12-geography-ug5-t1.overview: Multiple Faces of Poverty and Implication to Development sits inside Challenges of Economic Development. Economic development is the focus of Unit 5 of Grade 12 Geography in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it unpacks the many faces of poverty and how they hold back economic development. Then it weighs the gains and costs of globalization, the trade imbalance between rich and poor nations, the drag of corruption, and the toll of global health crises, before moving on to solutions to environmental and sustainability problems. Students will also learn how economic development applies to real-life situations.
objectives: Explain the causes and faces of poverty.
Assess the advantages and limitations of globalization for economic development.
Analyze how trade imbalance widens inequality between countries.
Describe the types and effects of corruption.
Evaluate the major global health crises and their impact.
g12-geography-ug5-t1.simple:
Multiple Faces of Poverty and Implication to Development in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the difference between absolute, relative and persistent poverty.
  • Then the structural and behavioural explanations of poverty.
  • Also the assets and dimensions that shape who stays poor.
  • Finally, how conflict and poverty feed each other.
g12-geography-ug5-t1.detailed:
Multiple Faces of Poverty and Implication to Development — the essentials. First, the difference between absolute, relative and persistent poverty. Then the structural and behavioural explanations of poverty. Also the assets and dimensions that shape who stays poor. Finally, how conflict and poverty feed each other.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Explain the causes and faces of poverty.
  • Assess the advantages and limitations of globalization for economic development.
  • Analyze how trade imbalance widens inequality between countries.
  • Describe the types and effects of corruption.
  • Evaluate the major global health crises and their impact.
